items.prompt: Which teeth are wide and flat for grinding food?

options.why: Incisors are at the front. They are sharp for cutting.
Canines are pointed for gripping and tearing.
Milk teeth are a child's first set of teeth, not one type.

hints: These teeth are at the back of your mouth.
Feel them with your tongue. Are they sharp or flat?
Think about which teeth mash rice and vegetables.
items.explanation: Molars are wide, flat teeth at the back of the mouth. They grind and crush food.

items.prompt: Match each type of tooth to its job.
hints: Think about where each tooth is in your mouth.
Front teeth bite into an apple.
Pointed teeth next to them grip.
items.explanation: Incisors cut and bite, canines grip and tear, and molars grind and chew.

items.prompt: How many milk teeth does a child usually have?
hints: Milk teeth are a child's first set of teeth.
Adults usually have 32 teeth. Children have fewer.
Count the top and bottom teeth in a young child's smile.
items.explanation: A child usually has 20 milk teeth. They fall out and are replaced by up to 32 adult teeth.

items.prompt: How does sugar make a hole in a tooth? Put the steps in order.
items: Sugary food stays on the teeth.
Bacteria in the mouth feed on the sugar.
The acid slowly makes a hole in the enamel.
hints: It starts with food left behind.
Tiny living things feed on the sugar.
The hole comes last.
items.explanation: Bacteria feed on sugar left on teeth and make acid. The acid slowly dissolves the enamel and makes a hole.

items.prompt: How often should you brush your teeth?

options.text: twice a day, for about two minutes

options.why: Plaque builds up every day, so brush every day.
By the time teeth hurt, damage is already done.
Water does not harm teeth. Twice a day is enough.

hints: Dentists give the same advice to everyone.
Think about morning and bedtime.
How long is a good, careful brush?
items.explanation: Brush twice a day, in the morning and before bed, for about two minutes. Use toothpaste with fluoride.

items.prompt: A cow has wide, flat teeth at the back of its mouth. What does a cow mostly eat?

options.why: Meat eaters have sharp, pointed teeth for tearing.
A cow's teeth are made for grinding plants.
Cows do not catch fish.

hints: Flat teeth grind food.
Tough food needs lots of grinding.
What do cows eat in a field?
items.explanation: Cows eat grass and other plants. Their wide, flat teeth grind tough plants into small pieces.

items.prompt: A lion has long, sharp canine teeth. What does it use them for?

options.why: Flat teeth grind grass. Lions do not eat grass.
Lions dig with their paws, not their teeth.
Flat back teeth are better for crushing.

hints: Lions are hunters.
Pointed teeth are good at holding on.
What kind of food does a hunter eat?
items.explanation: Lions eat meat. Their long, sharp canines grip prey and tear meat.

items.prompt: The hard, white outer layer of a tooth is called ___.
hints: It is the hardest material in your body.
Acid can damage it.
The word starts with e.
items.explanation: Enamel is the hard outer layer of a tooth. It protects the softer parts inside.

items.prompt: Choose 3 habits that help keep teeth healthy.

options.text: brushing twice a day with fluoride toothpaste

options.why: Sugar left on teeth at night feeds bacteria.
This can chip or crack your teeth.

options.text: drinking water instead of sweet drinks

hints: Think about sugar and bacteria.
Cross out habits that leave sugar on teeth or could break them.
Look for habits a dentist would praise.
items.explanation: Brushing with fluoride toothpaste, dentist check-ups and choosing water all protect teeth. Sweets before bed and opening bottles with teeth harm them.

items.prompt: Sort the animals by the main kind of teeth they have.
hints: Think about what each animal eats.
Meat eaters need teeth for gripping and tearing.
Plant eaters need teeth for grinding.
items.explanation: Lions, sharks and cats eat meat, so they have sharp, pointed teeth. Cows, horses and sheep eat plants, so they have flat, grinding teeth.

items.prompt: Why do children's milk teeth fall out?

options.why: Brushing keeps teeth healthy. It does not make them fall out.
Bacteria can make holes, but that is not why milk teeth fall out.
The jaw grows bigger, which makes room for adult teeth.

options.text: Bigger adult teeth grow underneath and push them out.

hints: Children's jaws get bigger as they grow.
Bigger jaws need bigger teeth.
Where do the new teeth come from?
items.explanation: Adult teeth grow in the jaw under the milk teeth. As they grow, they push the milk teeth out and take their place.

items.prompt: Ika leaves an eggshell in vinegar for two days. The shell goes soft. What does this model show about teeth?

options.text: Acid can damage the hard outer layer of teeth.

options.why: The shell went soft, so vinegar did not make it stronger.
The eggshell is just a model. The acid did the damage.
Eggshell and enamel are both hard, but the shell is only a model.

hints: Vinegar is an acid.
The eggshell is a model for something hard on teeth.
What do bacteria make that harms teeth?
items.explanation: Vinegar is an acid, and it softened the hard eggshell. In the same way, acid made by bacteria can damage tooth enamel.

items.prompt: Which teeth are at the front of the mouth and are used for cutting?

options.why: Molars are at the back and are used for grinding.
Premolars are behind the canines and crush and grind food.
Canines are pointed and used to tear food.

hints: These teeth are the first ones you see when you smile.
They have a thin, flat edge, like scissors.
Think about biting into an apple at the front.
items.explanation: Incisors are at the front. They have a thin edge for cutting food.

items.prompt: Label the parts of the tooth.

figure.alt: Cross-section of a tooth in the jaw. A hard shell covers the top part. Inside is a soft middle in a darker colour. Two roots go down into a pink area around the tooth.

hints: The hard outer layer protects the tooth.
The soft middle of the tooth has nerves.
The tooth is held in the pink part of the mouth.
items.explanation: Enamel is the hard outer shell. The pulp is the soft middle with nerves. The roots hold the tooth in the gum.

items.prompt: Tap the tooth that a lion uses to tear meat.

figure.alt: Four teeth in a row on a pink gum. From the left: a narrow flat tooth, a tall pointed tooth, a wider tooth with two bumps, and the widest tooth with four bumps.

hints: A lion needs a sharp point to grip and tear.
Look for the tooth with a single pointed tip.
This tooth is called a canine.
items.explanation: Canines are tall and pointed, so they grip and tear meat.

items.prompt: Match each animal to its teeth.
pairs: wide flat molars for grinding grass
hints: A meat eater needs teeth to tear.
A grass eater needs teeth to grind.
A rabbit gnaws on hard food.
items.explanation: Teeth are shaped for the food an animal eats.

items.prompt: 30 children say how often they brush each day. Fill in the missing number.
items.caption: Brushing in a day
head: Times brushed
Children
hints: The numbers in the table add up to 30.
Add the numbers you can see first.
Take that total away from 30.
items.explanation: 2 + 9 + 2 = 13, and 30 - 13 = 17. So 17 children brush twice a day.

items.prompt: Sekar leaves eggshells in four drinks for two days. The chart shows how soft each shell became. What does it show?

figure.alt: Bar chart of eggshell softness after two days. Water 1, milk 1, orange juice 4, fizzy drink 5.

options.text: The fizzy drink softened the shell most
The milk softened the shell most
options.why: Milk has the smallest bar, so it did the least harm.

options.text: The water softened the shell most
options.why: Water has a small bar. It did very little harm.

options.text: All the drinks softened the shell equally
options.why: The bars are different heights, so the drinks did different amounts of harm.

hints: The tallest bar shows the most softening.
Compare all four bars.
Find the drink with the tallest bar.
items.explanation: The fizzy drink has the tallest bar. Eggshell is a model for tooth enamel, so sugary and acid drinks can harm teeth.

items.prompt: Sekar tests drinks on eggshells. Sort each item.
hints: Change is the thing you alter on purpose.
Measure is what you record to compare results.
Everything else stays the same.
items.explanation: She changes the drink and measures how soft the shell gets. The time, shell size and amount of drink stay the same.

items.prompt: An adult has 32 teeth. There are 8 incisors, 4 canines and 8 premolars. The rest are molars. How many molars?
hints: Add the three types you know.
Take that total away from 32.

items.prompt: Kofi says, "Teeth are bones." Which fact shows he is wrong?

options.text: Teeth are white and bones are not
options.why: Colour alone does not decide what something is made of.

options.text: Teeth are in the head and bones are not
options.why: The skull is a bone and it is in the head.

options.text: Teeth can bend and bones cannot
options.why: Neither teeth nor bones bend easily.

options.text: A broken bone can mend itself but a broken tooth cannot

hints: Think about what living bones can do after an injury.
Compare how bone and tooth enamel repair.
Enamel cannot grow back once it is lost.
items.explanation: Bone is living and can repair itself. The hard enamel on a tooth cannot grow back, so teeth are not bones.

items.prompt: Pointed teeth that tear food are called ___.
hints: They are the pointed teeth in a dog or lion.
They sit next to the incisors.
The word starts with the letter c.
items.explanation: Canines are pointed and tear food.

items.prompt: Choose 2 snacks that are better for teeth.

options.why: Sticky sugar stays on teeth and feeds the germs that make holes.
It has sugar and acid, which harm tooth enamel.

hints: Sugar and acid harm teeth.
Look for snacks with no added sugar.
Choose the two snacks that are not sweet or fizzy.
items.explanation: Cheese and carrot sticks have no added sugar, so they are kinder to teeth.

items.prompt: Tom's rabbit has front teeth that never stop growing. What keeps them the right length?

options.why: Rabbits do not need a brush. They wear their teeth down by chewing.

options.text: They stop growing in adult rabbits
options.why: A rabbit's front teeth keep growing all its life.

options.text: Gnawing hard food wears them down

options.why: Water does not shorten teeth.

hints: Think about what a rabbit does with its front teeth.
Hard food rubs the teeth like sandpaper.
Which choice wears something away?
items.explanation: Rabbit front teeth keep growing. Chewing and gnawing hard food wears them down so they stay the right length.

items.prompt: Incisors ___ food and molars ___ it.
hints: Think about the shape of each tooth.
Incisors have a thin cutting edge.
Molars are wide and flat.
items.explanation: Incisors cut food and molars grind it.

items.prompt: Put the layers of a tooth in order, from the outside to the middle.
hints: The outside is the hardest layer.
The middle is soft and has nerves.
The layer under the enamel is dentine.
items.explanation: Hard enamel is on the outside, dentine is under it, and soft pulp is in the middle.

items.prompt: A scientist finds three skulls. Which animal ate both plants and meat?

head: Skull
Teeth found
rows: pointed canines and sharp back teeth
figure.alt: Table of three skulls. A has cutting incisors and flat molars. B has pointed canines and sharp back teeth. C has pointed canines and flat molars.

options.why: Flat molars and no pointed teeth mean it ate only plants.
Pointed canines and sharp back teeth mean it ate only meat.
One skull has teeth for both jobs.

hints: Meat eaters have pointed teeth.
Plant eaters have flat grinding teeth.
An animal that eats both needs both kinds.
items.explanation: Skull C has pointed canines for meat and flat molars for plants, so that animal ate both.

items.prompt: True or false: Incisors are the sharp, flat teeth at the front that cut food.
hints: Which teeth are at the very front?
They cut and slice.
Incisors cut.
items.explanation: Incisors work like scissors to bite off pieces of food, such as an apple.

items.prompt: True or false: Molars are the pointed teeth used for tearing meat.
hints: Which teeth are flat and wide?
Canines are the pointy ones.
Molars grind.
items.explanation: Canines are the pointed teeth for tearing. Molars are wide and flat at the back and are used for grinding food.

items.prompt: True or false: Brushing your teeth twice a day helps to stop tooth decay.
hints: What stays on teeth after meals?
Acid damages the enamel.
Brushing removes plaque.
items.explanation: Brushing removes plaque and sugar left on teeth. Plaque bacteria make acid that makes holes, called decay.

items.prompt: The sharp front teeth for biting food are ___.
hints: They are at the front of the mouth.
They cut and bite.
It starts with in.
items.explanation: Incisors are the sharp front teeth that cut food.
